extra.message: express-blinker is mounted for every request path using the images directory as its base. The middleware concatenates req.url to that base without normalization or containment checks, so traversal paths can read files outside images.

cwe: CWE-22: Path Traversal

extra.message: Uploads are accepted globally and validated only by the client-controlled filename extension. Arbitrary content named .png or .jpg is stored in the web-accessible images directory; /secret/postcheck also discloses the generated filename.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: The disk-writing upload middleware executes before the rate limiter at line 87. Even requests subsequently rejected by the limiter have already stored their files, allowing unauthenticated repeated uploads to exhaust disk space.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The id URL parameter is passed directly to eval(), allowing a crafted /home?id=... URL to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the application's origin.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code

extra.message: The nickname input is concatenated into HTML passed to jQuery.append(), allowing HTML and script-event injection. Console input is likewise passed to append()/html() without encoding at lines 171, 199, 208, and 216.

extra.message: The OAuth redirect page sends the Google access token to window.opener with targetOrigin '*'. A malicious origin that opens the OAuth flow can receive the token because the opener's origin is never validated.

cwe: CWE-346: Origin Validation Error

extra.message: The OAuth authorization request uses a constant state value, and neither the redirect page nor /auth/callback validates it. An attacker can initiate or substitute an OAuth response and cause login session swapping.

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery

extra.message: The JWT signing secret is hardcoded as 'hello'. Anyone with source access can forge authentication cookies containing arbitrary usernames and admin claims and access protected endpoints.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: Authentication JWTs are issued without an expiresIn option or exp claim and there is no server-side revocation. A stolen token remains usable indefinitely, including after logout.

extra.message: req.body.username and req.body.password are used directly as MongoDB query values. Because extended URL encoding accepts objects, inputs such as password[$ne]=x introduce MongoDB operators and bypass password authentication.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The email regex contains overlapping nested repetition: an unescaped wildcard followed by a + quantifier inside an outer * quantifier. A long non-matching email can trigger catastrophic backtracking and block the Node.js event loop.

cwe: CWE-1333: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity

extra.message: The prohibited @ninjasworkout.com domain is checked case-sensitively before the route lowercases and stores the address. An address such as user@NINJASWORKOUT.com bypasses the restriction and is then stored as the prohibited lowercase domain.

cwe: CWE-178: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity

extra.message: The posts route queries records for the user-controlled :username parameter but authorizes access merely by checking that the JWT contains any username. It never requires payload.username to equal req.params.username, so any authenticated user can read another user's posts.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Post ownership is derived from the process-global hello variable instead of req.user. Login overwrites global.hello at line 170, so one user's login changes the identity used by concurrent authenticated requests, causing cross-account post reads and writes.

cwe: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution Using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization

extra.message: The post quota is checked with a separate find() before save(). Concurrent requests can all observe result.length below the limit and then insert posts, bypassing the intended resource limit.

cwe: CWE-367: Time-of-check Time-of-use Race Condition

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery

extra.message: The password-recovery endpoint returns a distinct message when an email has no account and a reset-sent message when it exists. Attackers can enumerate registered email addresses from this observable difference.

cwe: CWE-203: Observable Discrepancy

cwe: CWE-346: Origin Validation Error
